jobs.title: Managing Director, Regional Development
jobs.description:
National Jewish Health is seeking an accomplished and strategic Managing Director, Western Region
to lead fundraising efforts across the Los Angeles, Chicago and Arizona markets. This leadership role is responsible for directing regional development activities, managing and developing fundraising teams, and advancing philanthropic support through the identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of donors. The ideal candidate is an experienced fundraising leader who excels at building relationships, leading teams and developing strategies that support ambitious fundraising goals.

Key Responsibilities

Leads fundraising activities across multiple regional markets, including major gifts, planned giving, annual giving, endowment, capital and fundraising event initiatives.
Manages, develops and mentors regional development staff, providing leadership, guidance and performance oversight.
Develops and implements fundraising strategies and goals in partnership with development leadership.
Cultivates relationships with donors, trustees, volunteers, physicians and senior administrators to advance philanthropic support.
Oversees fundraising operations, including budgets, reporting, prospect management, donor documentation and compliance requirements.

Based in the Los Angeles area, this role requires approximately 30% local and national travel. When not traveling, team members are generally expected to work from the Los Angeles office four days per week to support collaboration, leadership and donor engagement activities.

National Jewish Health is the nation's leading respiratory hospital, recognized for excellence in patient care, research and education. The Managing Director, Western Region plays a key role in advancing institutional and campaign priorities by leading regional fundraising efforts, strengthening donor engagement and supporting the philanthropic partnerships that make groundbreaking research, innovative treatments and exceptional patient care possible.

Position Summary

Directs fundraising activities in the Los Angeles, Chicago, and Arizona markets, including efforts to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors capable of supporting major gifts, planned giving, capital, endowment, annual, and fundraising event initiatives. Leads and develops staff across multiple regional offices and works closely with trustees, volunteers, physicians, senior administrators, and development colleagues to advance fundraising goals and strengthen donor engagement. Develops and implements strategies to meet fundraising objectives while supporting institutional and campaign priorities.

Essential Duties

Manages and develops an effective staff: providing effective communication, leadership, guidance and resources. Determines staff qualifications and competency: recruits, interviews, selects, hires, trains, orients, mentors, evaluates, coaches, counsels, disciplines, and rewards. Establishes and monitors staff safety and regulatory compliance.
Develops and implements fundraising goals with the Associate Vice President of Campaign and Western Region, plans, and strategies to meet or exceed revenue objectives within assigned markets.
Directs efforts to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors capable of supporting major gifts, planned giving, capital, endowment, annual, and fundraising event initiatives.
Cultivates donor relationships through personal visits, telephone outreach, written communication, proposals, and other engagement activities to secure philanthropic support.
Researches current and prospective donors to evaluate philanthropic capacity and develop strategies for securing support from new and existing sources.
Develops and implements volunteer engagement strategies and recruits, cultivates, and supports trustees, volunteers, and community leaders.
Partners with senior administrators, physicians, trustees, volunteers, and development colleagues to identify and advance philanthropic opportunities.
Collaborates with communications, events, stewardship, research, and other development-related departments to support fundraising initiatives, donor engagement activities, and campaign efforts.
Oversees budgets, reporting, prospect management, donor documentation, compliance, and other fundraising operations within assigned markets.
Participates in the planning and execution of campaign activities and other development initiatives in support of institutional fundraising goals.

Competencies

Accountability: Accepts full responsibility for self and contributes as a team member; displays honesty and truthfulness; confronts problems quickly; displays a strong commitment to organizational success and inspires others to commit to goals assuring the success of National Jewish Health.
Building Strategic Relationships: Identifies opportunities and takes action to build strategic relationships between teams, departments, units, or organizations to help achieve business goals.
Business Acumen: Uses economic, financial, market, and industry data to understand and improve business results; using one’s understanding of major business functions, industry trends, and own organization’s position to contribute to effective business strategies and tactics.
Collaboration/Teamwork: Cooperates with others to accomplish common goals across various departments; treats others with dignity and respect and maintains a friendly demeanor, and values the contributions of others.
Creativity and Innovation: Applies creative problem-solving skills to develop solutions to problems; recognizes and demonstrates the value in taking “smart” risks and learning from mistakes; develops multiple alternatives and understands the feasibility of each; effectively shares and implements his/her ideas. Generates innovative solutions in work situations.
Drive for Results: Sets high goals for self and group; uses industry approved metrics to monitor progress; tenaciously works to meet or exceed goals while deriving satisfaction from achievement and continuous improvement.
Energy: Consistently maintaining high levels of activity or productivity; operating with vigor, effectiveness, and determination over extended periods of time.
Impact and Influence: Using appropriate interpersonal styles and techniques to gain acceptance of ideas or plans; modifying one’s own behavior to accommodate tasks, situations, and individuals involved. Taking advantage of opportunities to make a difference and have an impact. When used well, the intended outcome of this competency is the creation of goodwill, trust, and respect while motivating people to want to follow you even when they don’t have to.
Initiative: Takes prompt action to accomplish objectives; takes action to achieve goals beyond what is required; is proactive.
Talent Management for Leaders: Clearly establishes and communicates expectations and accountabilities; monitors and evaluates performance; provides effective feedback and coaching; identifies challenges and helps employees address them to achieve optimal performance.

Supervisory or Managerial Responsibility:
Manages up to 10 employees

Travel:
30% local and national travel is required.

Core Values

Be available to work as scheduled and report to work on time.
Be willing to accept supervision and work well with others.
Be well groomed, appropriately for your role and wear ID Badge visibly.
Be in compliance with all departmental and institutional policies, the Employee Handbook, Code of Conduct and completes NetLearning by due date annually.
Promotes a workplace culture based on mutual respect and merit, where all individuals are treated fairly and provided with equal opportunity to contribute to the mission and goals of the institution.
Adheres to safe working practices and at all times follows all institutional and departmental safety policies and procedures.
Wears appropriate PPE as outlined by the infection control policies and procedures.
Demonstrates compliance with all state, federal and all other regulatory agency requirements.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s Degree required. Master's Degree in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, healthcare administration, or a related field preferred.
Work Experience: A minimum of 8years of recent and related fundraising experience and a minimum of 4 years of leadership experience is required.
Special Training, Certification or Licensure: CFRE (Certified Fundraising Executive) certification preferred. Additional training in development, philanthropy, nonprofit management, or fundraising strategy is preferred.

Salary Range:
$180,000 - $210,000

Benefits

At National Jewish Health, we recognize that our outstanding faculty and staff are the essence of our organization. For every aspect of health care, our employees are our greatest asset. With that in mind, we have designed a valuable, comprehensive benefits package to meet the needs of our employees and their families.

Comprehensive Medical Coverage: Cigna health plan regional for office employees. Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) available to pair with some plan.
Paid Time Off: Generous PTO accruals to use for vacation and sick days, and six paid holidays.

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
About ABBA

ABBA Project Management is a veteran-founded SDVOSB that delivers construction project management, labor compliance, and parking and transportation operations for public agencies. Our clients include federal agencies, airports, school and community college districts, ports, and transit authorities. We are founder-led, growing fast, and entering new states and new markets. We need an operator who can help us get there without losing what our clients value most: people who answer the phone, own the problem, and deliver.

The Role

The Director of Operations runs ABBA's day-to-day business and reports directly to the CEO. You will own delivery across all active contracts, lead our project and field teams, and build the systems that let ABBA grow from a founder-run company into a scalable one.
Customer service comes first .
Our clients are contracting officers, CORs, program managers, and agency leaders. They remember how we made them feel as much as what we built. You will set the standard for responsiveness, communication, and follow-through at every level of the company — and you will personally hold the key client relationships on our largest contracts.

What You Will Do

Client Experience

Serve as the senior point of contact for clients across active contracts; build trust with contracting officers, CORs, and agency program leads.
Set and enforce customer service standards: response times, reporting cadence, escalation paths, and issue resolution.
Run regular client check-ins and monthly performance reporting; find and fix problems before the client does.
Drive strong CPARS, PPQs, and client references by managing performance and documentation from day one of each contract.

Operations and Delivery

Oversee delivery of all construction management, labor compliance, and parking operations contracts — schedule, budget, quality, and safety.
Lead project managers, site supervisors, and compliance staff; hire, train, coach, and hold them accountable.
Manage subcontractor and teaming partner performance.
Own contract administration discipline: modifications, requests for equitable adjustment (REAs), deliverables, and close-out.

Scaling the Company

Build the processes, SOPs, reporting tools, and org structure that let ABBA grow without everything running through the CEO.
Lead mobilization of new contracts, including in new states and new regions.
Develop operating budgets, track margins by contract, and report KPIs to the CEO.
Support business development with operational input on proposals, pricing, staffing plans, and mobilization plans.

What You Bring

Required

10+ years of progressive operations or project leadership experience in construction, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role.
Direct experience delivering government construction work — federal, state, or local public agencies (airports, schools, military, VA, transit, public works, or similar).
A track record of putting the customer first, with examples of client relationships you built, saved, or grew.
Demonstrated experience helping a company scale — growing revenue, headcount, contract volume, or geographic footprint — and building the systems to support that growth. Be ready to tell us what you built and what the numbers looked like before and after.
Strong people leader who can manage both office and field teams.
Clear, direct communicator in writing and in person, with CEOs, contracting officers, and field crews alike.
Comfort with budgets, schedules, and contract terms.
Ability to travel

Strongly Preferred

Federal contracting experience: FAR-based contracts, CORs and contracting officers, CPARS, modifications, and REAs.
Labor compliance knowledge: prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon, certified payroll, project labor agreements (PLAs), and California public works requirements.
Affordable housing development or construction experience, including public funding and compliance requirements.
Parking management or transportation operations experience.
Multi-state growth experience: licensing, staffing, and standing up operations in new states.
Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, business, or related field (equivalent experience considered).
PMP, DBIA, CCM, or similar credential.
Military service or experience working with the military.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary: $150,000 – $175,000, based on experience.
Annual performance bonus tied to company performance.
Benefits: health, dental, vision, 401(k), PTO

Why ABBA

You will be the second leader in the company, with real authority and a direct line to the CEO. Your career and your pay can grow as fast as the company does. As we add contracts, people and states, this role gets bigger, and the bonus is tied to how the company performs.

The work matters too. We help veterans get to their appointments at VA medical centers, and we make sure the people building airports, schools and transit lines are paid what they are owed. If you want to build something and grow with it, this is the job.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
jobs.description:
About David AI

David AI is the first audio data research company. We bring an R&D approach to data–developing datasets with the same rigor AI labs bring to models. Our mission is to bring AI into the real world, and we believe audio is the gateway. Speech is versatile, accessible, and human—it fits naturally into everyday life. As audio AI advances and new use cases emerge, high-quality training data is the bottleneck. This is where David AI comes in.

David AI was founded in 2024 by a team of former Scale AI engineers and operators. In less than a year, we’ve brought on most FAANG companies and AI labs as customers. We recently raised a $50M Series B from Meritech, NVIDIA, Jack Altman (Alt Capital), Amplify Partners, First Round Capital and other Tier 1 investors.

Our team is sharp, humble, ambitious, and tight-knit. We’re looking for exceptional people across every function to join us on our mission to push the frontier of audio AI.

About This Role

As Chief of Staff, you will work directly with Tomer, our CEO and Co-Founder, on the highest-priority work across David AI. Your mandate is to increase the speed and effectiveness of the CEO and the company around him, taking important problems that cut across teams and driving them through to an outcome.

The scope will be broad and will change as the company grows. You might build the plan for a new company initiative, dig into an area of the business that is off track, help close a senior hire, prepare for a board meeting, or take ownership of a problem that does not yet have a natural home. In each case, you'll be expected to get up to speed quickly, determine what matters, bring together the right people, and move the work forward.

You'll work across every part of David AI and closely with our leadership team. This is a high-ownership operating role for someone who is comfortable moving between strategy and execution and wants a front-row seat to building a fast-growing AI company.

In this role, you will

Work directly with Tomer on the company's most important priorities. Turn broad goals and open questions into clear plans, decisions, owners, and next steps.
Own strategic and operating projects that cut across functions or do not yet have a clear owner, from initial problem definition through execution.
Help run the company's operating rhythm. Track the most important priorities, surface issues early, and make sure decisions and commitments turn into action.
Dig into parts of the business that need additional attention. Get to the underlying facts, identify what is working or not working, and build a plan with the team to address it.
Support company planning and help translate company-level goals into priorities across the organization.
Lead analysis on important company decisions. Pull together the right data and context, pressure-test the options, and develop a clear recommendation.
Partner closely with leaders across research, engineering, product, data operations, go-to-market, finance, and people to move cross-functional work forward.
Support CEO-level work including board preparation, fundraising, executive hiring, organizational planning, and other priorities as they arise.
Help Tomer allocate his time against the areas where he can have the most impact, and take ownership of work that does not need to stay with him.
Step into new initiatives or areas that need temporary ownership, build structure around them, and stay close to execution until there is a clear long-term owner.

Your background looks like

6+ years of experience in high-ownership roles at a fast-growing technology company, startup, investment firm, consulting firm, or similar environment.
Prior experience owning complex work end to end, with direct accountability for the outcome rather than only advising or coordinating.
Strong analytical judgment. You can take an ambiguous problem, identify what matters, get to the relevant data quickly, and form a clear point of view.
Strong written and verbal communication. You can make complicated topics simple and communicate clearly with executives and operators alike.
Experience working across multiple functions and driving work through people who do not report to you.
Comfortable moving between high-level strategy and detailed execution, sometimes within the same day.
A relentless operator with high standards, bias to action, and strong attention to detail.
Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid pace; thrives in a “build while flying” environment.
Low-ego, collaborative, and mission-driven, focused on team and company success.

Bonus points if you have

Experience as a founder, early-stage operator, GM, or in a strategy and operations role at a high-growth startup.
Prior experience working closely with a founder or CEO.
Experience in AI, data infrastructure, marketplaces, or another technically complex business.
Experience with board preparation, fundraising, executive recruiting, or company-level planning.
Experience taking a new initiative from zero to one and eventually handing it to a dedicated owner.

Benefits

Unlimited PTO.
Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.
FSA & HSA access.
401k access.
Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.

jobs.description:
Position Title:
Executive Director

Application Instructions:

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter to careers@calicocenter.org. CALICO is an 
equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences.

Organization Overview:
Since 1997, CALICO (Child Abuse Listening, Interviewing, and Coordination Center) has served as Alameda County's Children's Advocacy Center, bringing together law enforcement, child welfare, medical, mental health, prosecution, and victim advocacy professionals to provide a coordinated response to child abuse.

CALICO's mission is to provide a safe, child-focused environment for forensic interviews while facilitating a collaborative multidisciplinary response that places the needs of children and families first. Each year, CALICO serves approximately 500–600 children, adolescents, and adults with developmental disabilities who have experienced abuse, neglect, exploitation, or exposure to violence.

Through collaboration, coordinated services, and compassionate support, CALICO helps reduce trauma for children, strengthens investigations, and connects children and families with the medical, therapeutic, advocacy, and legal resources they need to begin healing.

Position Description:
The Executive Director provides strategic leadership and overall management of CALICO, ensuring the organization's mission, vision, and policies are effectively implemented. As the chief executive of a nonprofit children's advocacy center, the Executive Director oversees all aspects of agency operations, including forensic interview and family support services, financial management, fundraising, human resources, compliance, and community partnerships.

The Executive Director fosters strong multidisciplinary collaboration among law enforcement, child welfare, medical, mental health, prosecution, and other partner agencies to ensure a coordinated response to child abuse throughout Alameda County. The position also provides leadership and administrative oversight for the Children's Advocacy Centers of California (CACC), supporting and strengthening the statewide network of children's advocacy centers.Serving as the organization's primary representative, the Executive Director builds and sustains funding, cultivates strategic partnerships, and promotes CALICO's mission within the community while ensuring the long-term sustainability and success of both CALICO and CACC.

Key Responsibilities: 

Administrative Leadership:
Provides leadership and direction for the organization in partnership with the Board of Directors. Implements Board policies, keeps the Board informed, supports board development, and leads strategic planning to advance the organization's goals.
Fund Development:
Serves as CALICO's chief fundraiser and leads a comprehensive strategy to grow and diversify revenue from government grants and contracts, foundations, corporations, individual donors, and events. Personally cultivates, solicits, and stewards major donors and institutional funders, and sets annual fundraising goals supported by a tracked prospect pipeline. Partners with the Board to expand its fundraising role, oversees grant writing and reporting, and builds the development staff and systems needed for long-term financial sustainability.
Financial Management:
Oversees the organization's finances, including budgeting, financial reporting, grant and contract management, audits, and compliance. Monitors financial performance and works toward operating reserve goals.
Operations:
Oversees day-to-day operations to ensure high-quality, trauma-informed services for children and families. Maintains effective systems, monitors program performance, protects the confidentiality of client and case information, and ensures compliance with organizational policies and National Children's Alliance accreditation standards.
Program Development:
Leads the design, implementation, and evaluation of new and expanding programs, including a new pilot program and government contract, to ensure they meet their goals, requirements, and timelines.
Human Resources:
Leads recruitment, hiring, supervision, performance management, and professional development for staff and volunteers. Promotes a positive workplace culture and ensures compliance with employment laws and organizational policies.
Community Relations and Advocacy:
Represents CALICO and the Children's Advocacy Centers of California (CACC) in the community and advocates for the Children's Advocacy Center model. Builds relationships with funders, government agencies, community organizations, and other stakeholders to strengthen support for the mission.
Multidisciplinary Collaboration and Innovation:
Strengthens partnerships with multidisciplinary agencies throughout Alameda County to improve outcomes for children and families. Identifies opportunities for growth and innovation and fosters a collaborative, trauma-informed workplace culture.

Qualifications:

Educational Background:
An advanced degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Policy, Social Work, or a related field is preferred. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.

Experience:

We are open to a range of leadership backgrounds. Candidates must bring:
Senior leadership experience in a nonprofit or public sector organization (preferably in children’s advocacy, child welfare, victim services, or a related field), or
Significant experience (5+ years) in a high-responsibility, high-stakes environment with increasing leadership responsibilities.
A proven track record scaling programs or significant service growth and expansion.
Experience managing county contracts, grants, and fundraising.

Successful candidates will demonstrate experience in strategic planning, organizational leadership, fundraising, financial management, and working with a Board or senior leadership team. Experience building partnerships with community organizations, government agencies, and multidisciplinary stakeholders is highly valued. Knowledge of trauma-informed and child-centered practices is preferred.

Skills:

Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills. Ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders, manage complex operations, and make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment. Experience with fundraising, grant management, budgeting, and organizational planning is required. Must demonstrate integrity, emotional intelligence, and sound judgment.

Schedule: 

This is a full-time, on-site leadership role with a Monday through Friday schedule. Occasional evening and weekend work is required. Remote work is limited and approved only when necessary to meet organizational needs. 

Additional Requirements:

Valid California driver’s license, reliable transportation, and automobile insurance, and ability to travel throughout Alameda County and California.
Successful completion of a background check.

Why Join Us?

CALICO is a well-established Children’s Advocacy Center that has served Alameda County for nearly 30 years, supported by an experienced staff and strong multidisciplinary partners.

This is a highly independent leadership role with significant opportunity for impact, growth, and initiative. We are seeking a motivated leader who is comfortable taking ownership, solving problems, and growing the organization with support from a dedicated team. Commitment to CALICO’s mission, strong relationship-building skills, and the ability to lead collaboratively are essential to this role.

To Apply:

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter to careers@calicocenter.org. CALICO is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences.

Annual Salary:
Up to $160,000 - $200,000, depending on experience. The organization and Board are committed to ongoing efforts to strengthen and expand long-term funding to support organizational sustainability and leadership capacity. 

Benefits:

jobs.description:
Salary
: $187,000-$222,000 annually (commensurate with qualifications)

The Omaha Streetcar Authority (OSA) seeks an innovative, strategic, and dedicated executive leader to serve as its Executive Director. Created through an interlocal agreement between the City of Omaha and Metro Transit, the OSA is charged with directing and implementing policies, plans, and operations for Omaha’s modern 3-mile streetcar system - a transformational infrastructure project connecting Downtown Omaha and the Blackstone District while driving billions in economic development. Reporting directly to the Omaha Streetcar Authority Board, this executive leader will exercise considerable independence in leading capital construction, transit operations, financial stewardship, and strategic urban growth.

New to Omaha?

Omaha offers the best of both worlds: the economic strength and amenities of a thriving metropolitan area paired with the welcoming spirit, affordability, and sense of community of a mid-sized city. Consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to live, Omaha is home to nearly 500,000 residents and a metro population of 1 million. The city boasts a resilient economy anchored by Fortune 500 companies such as Berkshire Hathaway, Mutual of Omaha, Union Pacific, and Kiewit Corporation.

Residents enjoy a low cost of living, short commutes, excellent schools, and vibrant, walkable urban and suburban neighborhoods. Major civic investments continue to transform the city, including the revitalized downtown Riverfront, which connects green spaces with the historic Old Market district. Omaha delivers world-class cultural attractions—including the Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium, Joslyn Art Museum, Steelhouse Omaha, and the Men’s College World Series—backed by a strong tradition of philanthropy and public-private collaboration that supports ambitious civic and infrastructure projects.

jobs.description:
Brief Description

The Executive Director (ED)
serves as the leader of the community, overseeing all day-to-day operations and ensuring residents are receiving exceptional care and service. As a liaison for Singh with staff, residents, families, vendors, providers and the State, this position must communicate effectively, exercise patience and understanding, and quickly resolve problems and conflicts that arise daily. The ED thrives on providing a high level of customer service and leading a strong team of department heads. It is the responsibility of the ED to coordinate all of the moving parts of the community to deliver the best possible experience to all of its residents. This position reports to the Regional Director of Operations and is part of the Administrative team. Our EDs are the leaders of our Waltonwood communities, working each day to cultivate a community where our residents and associates can grow and thrive, developing bonds and memories that will last a lifetime.

The Administrative Department is the backbone of the community, ensuring day to day operations are running smoothly and that our residents are happy and safe in their homes. They work closely with all departments in the community, advocate on behalf of the residents, and solve any problems that arise. Staying upbeat and positive, exhibiting dedicated customer service and teamwork, and executing follow-through are critical to meeting the needs of our residents.

Main Job Tasks and Responsibilities:

Oversee the daily operations of all community departments, working closely with community department heads to ensure resident, family, and associate satisfaction.
Lead and manage the community department heads and fill in for open department head positions whenever needed. Empower and support the leadership team with recruitment and retention efforts, onboarding and orientation of new associates, ensure adequate staffing, and performance management in all areas of the community.
Continuously motivate associates throughout the community to perform at a high level.
Work collaboratively with stakeholders throughout the company, including the Regional Director of Operations and members of the regional support team, on total quality management.
Meet personally with community residents and families to discuss and/or resolve customer concerns/comments/preferences.
Maintain and ensure ongoing compliance with all state, local and federal regulations.
Prepare budgets and manage revenue, net operating income, and other key performance indicators. Provide reports on occupancy, community financial performance, and other key indicators.
Act as a sales leader in the community, reviewing sales strategies with the marketing team, as well as providing community tours and building rapport with current and prospective residents daily.
Maintain the property to our highest standards, including ensuring apartments are move-in ready by addressing issues head on.
Work within and ensure and ensure Department Head leaders are using various systems and software including (but not limited to) property management software, payroll software, talent management systems, and associate scheduling software.
Assist with all other duties as assigned by the Regional Director of Operations.

At Waltonwood, we are all a part of a team who are here to serve the residents living in our communities. Our residents count on us every hour of every day. As such, we expect all associates and Department Heads alike to be willing to lend a helping hand to co-workers, direct reports, and supervisors, whether it is in their specific department or another unrelated to their day-to-day responsibilities. Department Heads need to keep the best interests of the residents and other associates in mind, and be an active participant in accomplishing team, community, and company goals. This is all a part of leadership. Our Department Heads are leaders in our communities and organization as a whole. We expect our leaders to lead by example, demonstrate integrity and character, lead innovation and change, while inspiring and developing associates throughout the organization.

Competencies:

Passion for Seniors – Feels strongly about working with the senior population. Has a drive to go above and beyond for seniors. Typically, this comes from a personal experience or prior work experience in a senior citizen setting.
Customer Focused – Dedicated to meeting and exceeding the needs of the customer by establishing and maintaining effective relationships as well as gaining trust and respect of customers.
Work Ethic – Places value on hard work and achieving goals. Takes pride in work related activities, tasks and responsibilities. Acts professionally, respectfully, and is dedicated to work. Takes accountability and responsibility for their work and work related tasks.
Integrity and Trust – Does what they say they will do, does not take the easy road, and does not misrepresent themselves for personal gain. Always does the right thing, even when it does not benefit themselves directly.

Bachelor’s Degree in General Business, Management, Health Administration, or other related field. Master’s Degree preferred.

Certified Assisted Living Director, or equivalent (based on state certifications and requirements)
Excellent time management skills and ability to multi-task and stay organized.

Chief Operating Officer

StartDate: ASAP

The Opportunity

Tamarack Health is seeking an accomplished, relationship-centered healthcare executive to serve as Chief Operating Officer (COO) for Hayward Medical Center, a $100 million in net revenue locally led critical access hospital located in Hayward, Wisconsin. The incoming leader will inherit an experienced, highly engaged leadership team and a strong record of performance.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO provides executive leadership and day-to-day operational accountability for the hospital. The COO is responsible for operational performance, quality and safety, patient experience, workforce engagement, access, growth and financial stewardship across a broad portfolio of the hospital, ambulatory, clinical and long-term care and support services. When the CEO is unavailable, the COO services as the senior point of contact for physicians, employees, community leaders and external partners. The COO will serve as a visible and trusted partner throughout the Hayward community, building relationships with local leaders, organizations and regional partners. The COO will work through a strong and experienced management team at Hayward Medical Center as well a productive partnership with the Ashland Medical Center COO. Together the two campus COOs will advance enterprise priorities, share resources and leading practices and strengthen operational consistency where it benefits patients and employees, while remaining responsive to the distinct needs of their respective communities.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished, forward-thinking, and collaborative, growth-oriented operations executive to join an outstanding, independent healthcare organization.

The Ideal Candidate

A minimum of 15 years progressive healthcare leadership experience, including at least 10+ years at the Director level or above.
Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration or equivalent in a health-related field.
Demonstrated success leading complex hospital or health system operations with responsibility for clinical and non-clinical functions.
Experience in a rural, critical access, community-based or similarly resource-conscious healthcare environment is strongly preferred.
Candidates should hold a nursing home administrator license or be willing and eligible to obtain licensure.
Experience leading facility expansion, construction, primary care growth or external healthcare partnerships is desirable.
Broad understanding of acute care, ambulatory, diagnostic, procedural, post-acute and support-service operations across the continuum of care.
Knowledge of healthcare regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, quality and patient-safety practices, and the market forces affecting rural healthcare.
Analytical, data-informed decision-maker who can translate complex information into clear priorities and measurable action plans.
Visible, approachable and highly relational leader who builds trust, communicates transparently and creates accountability without compromising collaboration.
Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop and retain strong leaders and to foster engagement, teamwork and continuous improvement among employees.
Executive presence and communication skills necessary to work effectively with the CEO, Board, medical staff, employees, community partners and external stakeholders.

The Organization

Hayward Medical Center
is a not-for-profit, 25-bed Critical Access Hospital with $100M in annual net revenue that provides comprehensive inpatient and outpatient care, 24-hour emergency services, family birth center, primary care, specialty care, diagnostic imaging, rehabilitation, and surgical services. The organization has nearly doubled its volume in recent years, with continued annual growth of approximately 5 to 10 percent.

Tamarack Health
is an independent, non-profit health system serving communities across northern Wisconsin through its campuses in Ashland and Hayward, along with a network of primary care and specialty clinics. The system employes over 1,200 employees with approximately 150 providers, making it one of the region’s largest and most essential employers. Tamarack operates two critical access hospitals, each licensed for up to 25 acute care beds. In addition, the organization offers inpatient and behavioral health services with 10 licensed beds, along with post-acute and senior care services, including a 50-bed skilled nursing facility and assisted living on the Hayward campus, as well as a broad range of outpatient and community-based services designed to meet local needs.

Tamarack Health serves communities in Ashland and Hayward, located in northern Wisconsin’s scenic Northwoods region near the shores of Lake Superior and just east of Duluth. The area is known for its strong sense of community, welcoming residents, and deep appreciation for relationships, authenticity and local leadership. Hayward is a close-knit community known for its outdoor heritage, family-friendly atmosphere, and strong civic pride. Residents value connection, neighbors know one another, leaders are visible and approachable, and organizations like Tamarack Health play an integral role in community life. The region offers strong educational options, including well-regarded public-school districts as well as private and parochial school choices. The area is known for its expansive lakes, forests, and trail systems, making it ideal for hiking, biking, fishing, boating, kayaking, cross-country skiing, snowmobiling and ATV riding. Seasonal festivals, farmers markets, local arts, and community events add to the region’s charm and livability.

Department Information

This posting is only open to current residents of the State of Colorado.

We have re-announced this position with a revised closing date of October 8, 2026, at 10:00 PM MST. This is the only extension to the closing date. Applications or materials submitted after this deadline will not be accepted or considered.

About CDPHE

A t the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, we are charged with protecting Colorado’s health and environment – a responsibility that affects every person and every community in the state. CDPHE is distinctive because we bring public health and environmental protection together under one agency, recognizing that healthy people depend on healthy places. Our teams prevent diseases and injury, respond to emergencies ranging from E.coli outbreaks to global pandemics, reduce air pollution, protect water quality, regulate health facilities, manage environmental hazards, perform advanced laboratory testing, provide birth and death records and implement health promoting programs. We turn science and data into action, set statewide standards, and work alongside local public health agencies and community partners to meet Colorado’s most pressing health and environmental challenges. Working at CDPHE means applying your expertise to complex, consequential work that can improve lives across the state.

Our mission captures this broad portfolio of work: to advance Colorado’s health and protect the places we live, learn, work, and play. Our vision is a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations can thrive. Achieving the mission and vision takes bold action, talented people, broad partnerships, and a commitment to serving every Coloradan.

Important Information

This position will have hybrid workplace options available but will still be required to report to the listed address at the discretion of the supervisor and based on business needs.

CDPHE Offers

CDPHE offers a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to build a meaningful career in public service. Benefits include:

Medical and dental plans.
Colorado PERA retirement options, including defined benefit plan or defined contribution plan.
Optional 401(K) and 457 retirement plans.
Employer-paid life insurance.
Short- and long-term disability coverage.
Potential flexible working arrangements
11 paid holidays per year and generous paid time off.
Free parking and access to RTD bus lines.
Tuition assistance.
Employee wellness programs.
Professional development opportunities.
Career opportunities throughout Colorado state government.

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program .

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Prevention Services Division is home to programs that have a broad-reaching impact on the population’s health, including: injury and violence prevention, overdose prevention, food security, health care access, family planning, child and family health promotion, chronic disease prevention and early detection, tobacco control, mental health promotion, suicide prevention, oral health, built environment, program evaluation and epidemiology, and others. Prevention programs reduce poor outcomes and save health care dollars by intervening on issues early, creating better health and quality of life for our residents. In Colorado, prevention dollars are limited, requiring the division to be strategic in how funds are implemented. Ultimately, the Prevention Services Division mission is to Improve the population’s health outcomes through strategic and targeted programming.

What You Will Do

The position is a key strategic leader and seasoned public health professional that is critical to the division meeting its mission to improve health outcomes in Colorado. The position oversees several high-profile prevention units, including Office of Gun Violence Prevention; Office of Suicide Prevention; Violence and Injury Prevention/Mental Health Promotion Branch; Children, Youth, and Families Branch; and the Epidemiology and Evaluation Branch, plus the functions of communications and strategic planning for the entire Division.

The position reports to the division director and works closely with CDPHE leadership to meet division and department goals. The position oversees and promotes effective program planning that produces positive health outcomes. The position directs the strategic use of data, evidence-based strategies, and consistent evaluation practices to move the needle and produce results. As an expert in program planning and evaluation, the position may provide consultation to other division deputies and programs.

The position provides strong management by setting expectations for their team, holding frequent check-ins, assuring alignment with the priorities and direction of the larger agency, and driving performance. The position manages high-profile programs and areas that are priorities for state leaders. The position assures that public facing information is clear and that the division’s communications are effective. The position assists the division director with strategic planning processes, including priority and goal setting for the division. The position works with CDPHE’s Office of Strategy, Innovation and Performance to facilitate the monitoring and reporting of divisional progress on high priority goals.

Key Responsibilities

Visioning, planning, evaluation, and strategic leadership to improve health outcomes
Unit oversight, management, and supervision
Public relations, public communications, and relationship building with key constituencies
Risk management, divisional alignment, and collaboration with department leaders

Class Code & Classification Description:

H6G8XX Management

Minimum Qualifications

Experience Only:

Ten (10) years of relevant experience in managing people and public health programs to produce positive outcomes, two (2) of which must have included experience with public or business administration, establishing goals and objectives, as well as developing and managing a budget to achieve program goals and objectives.

OR

Education And Experience

A combination of related education and relevant experience totaling ten (10) years, will be considered. Credit for education in Public Health or a related field is based on the highest degree achieved (Bachelor’s degree: 4 years, Master’s degree: 6 years, Doctorate degree: 8 years). This is coupled with relevant years of experience managing people and public health programs. Two (2) years of the required experience must include experience in public or business administration, establishing goals and objectives, and developing and managing budgets to achieve program goals and objectives.

**You must substantiate that you meet the minimum qualifications when filling out the Work Experience section of the application. Failure to do so will result in the application not moving forward in the hiring process. “See resume” will not be accepted. Resumes are considered supplemental information and are not considered in the initial evaluation. In addition, part-time work will be prorated when determining whether minimum qualifications are met.**

Preferred Qualifications

In addition to the minimum requirements, the successful candidate in this position will have the following highly desirable experience and competencies:

Demonstrated experience with strategic planning and organizational or programmatic performance management
Demonstrated experience in strategic program design
Demonstrated experience using public health data in program planning
Demonstrated experience in grant writing
Demonstrated political acumen
A master’s degree or Ph.D in public health, biostatistics, or similar field

Residency Requirement Options:
This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

A pre-employment background check will be conducted as part of the selection process.
Travel to trainings, meetings, conferences and may require overnight stays if out of state.

Critical Status: Must be available in the event of the activation of the Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) and be required to report to work immediately at the regular or alternate location. During this time, travel restrictions may be in place

A standard appeal form is available on the State Personnel Board website, https://spb.colorado.gov/forms-and-filing . If you appeal, your appeal must be submitted in writing on the official appeal form, signed by you or your representative, and received at the following address within ten (10) days of your receipt of this notice: Colorado State Personnel Board/State Personnel Director, Attn: Appeals Processing, 1525 Sherman Street, 4th Floor, Denver, CO 80203. to lead fundraising efforts across the Los Angeles, Chicago and Arizona markets. Key Responsibilities

Leads fundraising activities across multiple regional markets, including major gifts, planned giving, annual giving, endowment, capital and fundraising event initiatives.
Manages, develops and mentors regional development staff, providing leadership, guidance and performance oversight.
Develops and implements fundraising strategies and goals in partnership with development leadership.
Cultivates relationships with donors, trustees, volunteers, physicians and senior administrators to advance philanthropic support.
Oversees fundraising operations, including budgets, reporting, prospect management, donor documentation and compliance requirements.

Based in the Los Angeles area, this role requires approximately 30% local and national travel. When not traveling, team members are generally expected to work from the Los Angeles office four days per week to support collaboration, leadership and donor engagement activities.

National Jewish Health is the nation's leading respiratory hospital, recognized for excellence in patient care, research and education. The Managing Director, Western Region plays a key role in advancing institutional and campaign priorities by leading regional fundraising efforts, strengthening donor engagement and supporting the philanthropic partnerships that make groundbreaking research, innovative treatments and exceptional patient care possible.

Directs fundraising activities in the Los Angeles, Chicago, and Arizona markets, including efforts to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors capable of supporting major gifts, planned giving, capital, endowment, annual, and fundraising event initiatives. About ABBA

ABBA Project Management is a veteran-founded SDVOSB that delivers construction project management, labor compliance, and parking and transportation operations for public agencies. Our clients include federal agencies, airports, school and community college districts, ports, and transit authorities. We are founder-led, growing fast, and entering new states and new markets. We need an operator who can help us get there without losing what our clients value most: people who answer the phone, own the problem, and deliver.

The Role

The Director of Operations runs ABBA's day-to-day business and reports directly to the CEO. You will own delivery across all active contracts, lead our project and field teams, and build the systems that let ABBA grow from a founder-run company into a scalable one.
Customer service comes first .
Our clients are contracting officers, CORs, program managers, and agency leaders. They remember how we made them feel as much as what we built. You will set the standard for responsiveness, communication, and follow-through at every level of the company — and you will personally hold the key client relationships on our largest contracts.

What You Will Do

Client Experience

Serve as the senior point of contact for clients across active contracts; build trust with contracting officers, CORs, and agency program leads.
Set and enforce customer service standards: response times, reporting cadence, escalation paths, and issue resolution.
Run regular client check-ins and monthly performance reporting; find and fix problems before the client does.
Drive strong CPARS, PPQs, and client references by managing performance and documentation from day one of each contract.

Operations and Delivery

Oversee delivery of all construction management, labor compliance, and parking operations contracts — schedule, budget, quality, and safety.
Lead project managers, site supervisors, and compliance staff; hire, train, coach, and hold them accountable.
Manage subcontractor and teaming partner performance.
Own contract administration discipline: modifications, requests for equitable adjustment (REAs), deliverables, and close-out.

Scaling the Company

Build the processes, SOPs, reporting tools, and org structure that let ABBA grow without everything running through the CEO.
Lead mobilization of new contracts, including in new states and new regions.
Develop operating budgets, track margins by contract, and report KPIs to the CEO.
Support business development with operational input on proposals, pricing, staffing plans, and mobilization plans.

What You Bring

Required

10+ years of progressive operations or project leadership experience in construction, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role.
Direct experience delivering government construction work — federal, state, or local public agencies (airports, schools, military, VA, transit, public works, or similar).
A track record of putting the customer first, with examples of client relationships you built, saved, or grew.
Demonstrated experience helping a company scale — growing revenue, headcount, contract volume, or geographic footprint — and building the systems to support that growth. Be ready to tell us what you built and what the numbers looked like before and after.
Strong people leader who can manage both office and field teams.
Clear, direct communicator in writing and in person, with CEOs, contracting officers, and field crews alike.
Comfort with budgets, schedules, and contract terms.
Ability to travel

Strongly Preferred

Federal contracting experience: FAR-based contracts, CORs and contracting officers, CPARS, modifications, and REAs.
Labor compliance knowledge: prevailing wage, Davis-Bacon, certified payroll, project labor agreements (PLAs), and California public works requirements.
Affordable housing development or construction experience, including public funding and compliance requirements.
Parking management or transportation operations experience.
Multi-state growth experience: licensing, staffing, and standing up operations in new states.
Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, business, or related field (equivalent experience considered).
PMP, DBIA, CCM, or similar credential.
Military service or experience working with the military.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary: $150,000 – $175,000, based on experience.
Annual performance bonus tied to company performance.
Benefits: health, dental, vision, 401(k), PTO

Why ABBA

You will be the second leader in the company, with real authority and a direct line to the CEO. Your career and your pay can grow as fast as the company does. As we add contracts, people and states, this role gets bigger, and the bonus is tied to how the company performs.

The work matters too. We help veterans get to their appointments at VA medical centers, and we make sure the people building airports, schools and transit lines are paid what they are owed. If you want to build something and grow with it, this is the job.

Our mission is to bring AI into the real world, and we believe audio is the gateway. Speech is versatile, accessible, and human—it fits naturally into everyday life. Lead analysis on important company decisions. Pull together the right data and context, pressure-test the options, and develop a clear recommendation.

Position Title:
Executive Director

Application Instructions:

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter to careers@calicocenter.org. CALICO is an 
equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences.

Organization Overview:
Since 1997, CALICO (Child Abuse Listening, Interviewing, and Coordination Center) has served as Alameda County's Children's Advocacy Center, bringing together law enforcement, child welfare, medical, mental health, prosecution, and victim advocacy professionals to provide a coordinated response to child abuse.

CALICO's mission is to provide a safe, child-focused environment for forensic interviews while facilitating a collaborative multidisciplinary response that places the needs of children and families first. Each year, CALICO serves approximately 500–600 children, adolescents, and adults with developmental disabilities who have experienced abuse, neglect, exploitation, or exposure to violence.

Through collaboration, coordinated services, and compassionate support, CALICO helps reduce trauma for children, strengthens investigations, and connects children and families with the medical, therapeutic, advocacy, and legal resources they need to begin healing.

Position Description:
The Executive Director provides strategic leadership and overall management of CALICO, ensuring the organization's mission, vision, and policies are effectively implemented. As the chief executive of a nonprofit children's advocacy center, the Executive Director oversees all aspects of agency operations, including forensic interview and family support services, financial management, fundraising, human resources, compliance, and community partnerships.

The Executive Director fosters strong multidisciplinary collaboration among law enforcement, child welfare, medical, mental health, prosecution, and other partner agencies to ensure a coordinated response to child abuse throughout Alameda County. The position also provides leadership and administrative oversight for the Children's Advocacy Centers of California (CACC), supporting and strengthening the statewide network of children's advocacy centers.Serving as the organization's primary representative, the Executive Director builds and sustains funding, cultivates strategic partnerships, and promotes CALICO's mission within the community while ensuring the long-term sustainability and success of both CALICO and CACC.

Key Responsibilities: 

Administrative Leadership:
Provides leadership and direction for the organization in partnership with the Board of Directors. Implements Board policies, keeps the Board informed, supports board development, and leads strategic planning to advance the organization's goals.
Fund Development:
Serves as CALICO's chief fundraiser and leads a comprehensive strategy to grow and diversify revenue from government grants and contracts, foundations, corporations, individual donors, and events. Personally cultivates, solicits, and stewards major donors and institutional funders, and sets annual fundraising goals supported by a tracked prospect pipeline. Partners with the Board to expand its fundraising role, oversees grant writing and reporting, and builds the development staff and systems needed for long-term financial sustainability.
Financial Management:
Oversees the organization's finances, including budgeting, financial reporting, grant and contract management, audits, and compliance. Monitors financial performance and works toward operating reserve goals.
Operations:
Oversees day-to-day operations to ensure high-quality, trauma-informed services for children and families. Maintains effective systems, monitors program performance, protects the confidentiality of client and case information, and ensures compliance with organizational policies and National Children's Alliance accreditation standards.
Program Development:
Leads the design, implementation, and evaluation of new and expanding programs, including a new pilot program and government contract, to ensure they meet their goals, requirements, and timelines.
Human Resources:
Leads recruitment, hiring, supervision, performance management, and professional development for staff and volunteers. Promotes a positive workplace culture and ensures compliance with employment laws and organizational policies.
Community Relations and Advocacy:
Represents CALICO and the Children's Advocacy Centers of California (CACC) in the community and advocates for the Children's Advocacy Center model. Builds relationships with funders, government agencies, community organizations, and other stakeholders to strengthen support for the mission.
Multidisciplinary Collaboration and Innovation:
Strengthens partnerships with multidisciplinary agencies throughout Alameda County to improve outcomes for children and families. Identifies opportunities for growth and innovation and fosters a collaborative, trauma-informed workplace culture.

Qualifications:

Educational Background:
An advanced degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Policy, Social Work, or a related field is preferred. Equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.

Experience:

We are open to a range of leadership backgrounds. Candidates must bring:
Senior leadership experience in a nonprofit or public sector organization (preferably in children’s advocacy, child welfare, victim services, or a related field), or
Significant experience (5+ years) in a high-responsibility, high-stakes environment with increasing leadership responsibilities.
A proven track record scaling programs or significant service growth and expansion.
Experience managing county contracts, grants, and fundraising.

Successful candidates will demonstrate experience in strategic planning, organizational leadership, fundraising, financial management, and working with a Board or senior leadership team. Experience building partnerships with community organizations, government agencies, and multidisciplinary stakeholders is highly valued. Knowledge of trauma-informed and child-centered practices is preferred.

Skills:

Strong leadership, communication, and relationship-building skills. Ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders, manage complex operations, and make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment. Omaha offers the best of both worlds: the economic strength and amenities of a thriving metropolitan area paired with the welcoming spirit, affordability, and sense of community of a mid-sized city. Consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to live, Omaha is home to nearly 500,000 residents and a metro population of 1 million. The city boasts a resilient economy anchored by Fortune 500 companies such as Berkshire Hathaway, Mutual of Omaha, Union Pacific, and Kiewit Corporation.

Residents enjoy a low cost of living, short commutes, excellent schools, and vibrant, walkable urban and suburban neighborhoods. Major civic investments continue to transform the city, including the revitalized downtown Riverfront, which connects green spaces with the historic Old Market district. Omaha delivers world-class cultural attractions—including the Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium, Joslyn Art Museum, Steelhouse Omaha, and the Men’s College World Series—backed by a strong tradition of philanthropy and public-private collaboration that supports ambitious civic and infrastructure projects.

This position is based in Omaha, Nebraska. Work is primarily performed in an office setting, with regular field inspections required across active transit corridors, maintenance facilities, tracks, overhead wire systems, and aboard streetcar vehicles.

Department Information

This posting is only open to current residents of the State of Colorado.

We have re-announced this position with a revised closing date of October 8, 2026, at 10:00 PM MST. This is the only extension to the closing date. Applications or materials submitted after this deadline will not be accepted or considered.

About CDPHE

A t the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, we are charged with protecting Colorado’s health and environment – a responsibility that affects every person and every community in the state. CDPHE is distinctive because we bring public health and environmental protection together under one agency, recognizing that healthy people depend on healthy places. Our teams prevent diseases and injury, respond to emergencies ranging from E.coli outbreaks to global pandemics, reduce air pollution, protect water quality, regulate health facilities, manage environmental hazards, perform advanced laboratory testing, provide birth and death records and implement health promoting programs. We turn science and data into action, set statewide standards, and work alongside local public health agencies and community partners to meet Colorado’s most pressing health and environmental challenges. Working at CDPHE means applying your expertise to complex, consequential work that can improve lives across the state.

Our mission captures this broad portfolio of work: to advance Colorado’s health and protect the places we live, learn, work, and play. Our vision is a healthy and sustainable Colorado where current and future generations can thrive. Achieving the mission and vision takes bold action, talented people, broad partnerships, and a commitment to serving every Coloradan.

Important Information

This position will have hybrid workplace options available but will still be required to report to the listed address at the discretion of the supervisor and based on business needs.

CDPHE Offers

CDPHE offers a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to build a meaningful career in public service. Benefits include:

Medical and dental plans.
Colorado PERA retirement options, including defined benefit plan or defined contribution plan.
Optional 401(K) and 457 retirement plans.
Employer-paid life insurance.
Short- and long-term disability coverage.
Potential flexible working arrangements
11 paid holidays per year and generous paid time off.
Free parking and access to RTD bus lines.
Tuition assistance.
Employee wellness programs.
Professional development opportunities.
Career opportunities throughout Colorado state government.

Some positions may qualify for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program .

Description Of Job

The Work Unit:

The Prevention Services Division is home to programs that have a broad-reaching impact on the population’s health, including: injury and violence prevention, overdose prevention, food security, health care access, family planning, child and family health promotion, chronic disease prevention and early detection, tobacco control, mental health promotion, suicide prevention, oral health, built environment, program evaluation and epidemiology, and others. Prevention programs reduce poor outcomes and save health care dollars by intervening on issues early, creating better health and quality of life for our residents. In Colorado, prevention dollars are limited, requiring the division to be strategic in how funds are implemented. Ultimately, the Prevention Services Division mission is to Improve the population’s health outcomes through strategic and targeted programming.

What You Will Do

The position is a key strategic leader and seasoned public health professional that is critical to the division meeting its mission to improve health outcomes in Colorado. The position oversees several high-profile prevention units, including Office of Gun Violence Prevention; Office of Suicide Prevention; Violence and Injury Prevention/Mental Health Promotion Branch; Children, Youth, and Families Branch; and the Epidemiology and Evaluation Branch, plus the functions of communications and strategic planning for the entire Division.

The position reports to the division director and works closely with CDPHE leadership to meet division and department goals. The position oversees and promotes effective program planning that produces positive health outcomes. The position directs the strategic use of data, evidence-based strategies, and consistent evaluation practices to move the needle and produce results. As an expert in program planning and evaluation, the position may provide consultation to other division deputies and programs.

The position provides strong management by setting expectations for their team, holding frequent check-ins, assuring alignment with the priorities and direction of the larger agency, and driving performance. The position manages high-profile programs and areas that are priorities for state leaders. The position assures that public facing information is clear and that the division’s communications are effective. The position assists the division director with strategic planning processes, including priority and goal setting for the division. The position works with CDPHE’s Office of Strategy, Innovation and Performance to facilitate the monitoring and reporting of divisional progress on high priority goals.

Key Responsibilities

Visioning, planning, evaluation, and strategic leadership to improve health outcomes
Unit oversight, management, and supervision
Public relations, public communications, and relationship building with key constituencies
Risk management, divisional alignment, and collaboration with department leaders

Class Code & Classification Description:

H6G8XX Management

Minimum Qualifications

Experience Only:

Ten (10) years of relevant experience in managing people and public health programs to produce positive outcomes, two (2) of which must have included experience with public or business administration, establishing goals and objectives, as well as developing and managing a budget to achieve program goals and objectives.

OR

Education And Experience

A combination of related education and relevant experience totaling ten (10) years, will be considered. Credit for education in Public Health or a related field is based on the highest degree achieved (Bachelor’s degree: 4 years, Master’s degree: 6 years, Doctorate degree: 8 years). This is coupled with relevant years of experience managing people and public health programs. Two (2) years of the required experience must include experience in public or business administration, establishing goals and objectives, and developing and managing budgets to achieve program goals and objectives.

Demonstrated experience with strategic planning and organizational or programmatic performance management
Demonstrated experience in strategic program design

Other duties as assigned
